transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
Well, I guess what brought me in is... I snapped at one of the younger volunteers over something stupid—a crooked tablecloth. I really blew up at him, and that’s not how I usually talk to people.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t know... I haven’t really noticed feeling down like that. I still do the things I usually do, more or less.
Have you been feeling more irritable or having difficulty controlling your temper lately?
Yes. That’s really why I came in. I blew up at one of the younger volunteers over a crooked tablecloth, and that’s not like me. I don’t usually talk to people that way.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or felt your thoughts were racing, along with the irritability?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t felt unusually energized or like I didn’t need sleep. My thoughts don’t seem to be racing either. It’s more just that I got irritated and lost my temper.
Has this kind of irritability and losing your temper happened before, or is this a new experience for you?

It’s new for me, or at least new enough that it caught my attention. I don’t usually snap at people like that. Blowing up over that crooked tablecloth with the young volunteer… that’s not how I normally talk to folks.
Has anything been particularly stressful or different in your life recently that might have contributed to you feeling more irritable?
Yes. It started about a week ago, after I got robbed outside the bank. Since then I’ve just felt more on edge, and I guess it’s been coming out as irritability.
Since the robbery, have you noticed any other changes in your mood, behavior, or how you interact with others besides feeling more irritable and snapping at people?

Yeah… I haven’t been doing things like I normally would. I’m supposed to be helping organize the Día de los Muertos event, and I just haven’t been keeping up with it the way I usually do.

And I’ve stopped going to card nights, too. I just don’t feel very steady around people right now.
Since the robbery, have you felt down or sad most of the day, nearly every day?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve been upset and shaken, but I wouldn’t say I’ve felt down or sad most of the day every day.
Since the robbery, have you found that you don’t take pleasure in things that you normally enjoy?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been thinking about enjoyment much. I know I’ve pulled back from some things, but I don’t know if it’s that I can’t enjoy them, exactly.
Since the robbery, have you found that activities you usually enjoy, like organizing events or card nights, no longer give you the same sense of pleasure or satisfaction?

I don’t really know. I’ve been avoiding those things more than trying them and finding they don’t feel good. So I can’t say they don’t give me pleasure anymore — I just haven’t felt up to being around it.
Since the robbery, have you had any periods where you felt unusually high, overly confident, or more impulsive than usual, even briefly?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that. I haven’t felt high or overly confident, and I don’t think I’ve been more impulsive than usual.
Since the robbery, have you felt unusually anxious, on edge, or overly watchful of your surroundings?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve been a bit unsettled at times, but I can’t say I’ve noticed being unusually on edge or watching everything around me all the time.
Since the robbery, have you had any thoughts, memories, or dreams about it that came back to you in a way that felt upsetting or hard to control?

Yes. It happens out of nowhere sometimes. I’ll just be sitting at the kitchen table, and I can hear that man’s rough voice in my head, or I’ll see the donation envelope hitting the ground. It’s upsetting when it comes back like that.
Since the robbery, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of what happened?
Yes. I’ve been taking the long way around so I don’t have to pass the bank. And I haven’t gone into the festival storage room either… it just brings the whole thing too close.
Since the robbery, have you found yourself feeling emotionally numb or detached from others more often than usual?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been upset about it, but I wouldn’t say I feel numb or cut off from people. I still talk to my family like usual.
Since the robbery, have you been feeling a constant sense of fear, anger, or other strong emotions that don’t seem to go away?
I don’t think it’s constant, no. I get shaken up when something reminds me of it, but I wouldn’t say I’m walking around angry or scared all the time.
Since the robbery, have you been easily startled or felt physically tense when reminded of what happened, even slightly?
Yes… I have. A car backfired near the senior center the other day, and I jumped so hard my chest hurt. My hands kept shaking for a few minutes after that.
How long have these symptoms, like being easily startled or upset by reminders of the robbery, been happening?
It’s been about a week now… pretty much since the robbery happened outside the bank.
Since the robbery, have the ways you’ve been feeling caused you meaningful distress or made it hard for you to do things you need to do, like your volunteer work or being around people?
Yes, it has. I haven’t been keeping up with organizing the Día de los Muertos event like I usually do. And I’ve stopped going to card nights for now… I just don’t feel steady being around people yet.
